draft.title: Reduce, reuse and recycle
card: use less in the first place, such as buying only what you need.
use an item again, either for the same job or a new one, such as refilling a drink bottle.
break down used materials, such as aluminium, paper and plastic, and make them into new products.
All three save resources and energy. Scientists keep finding new ways to recycle materials.
draft.remember: Reduce uses less, reuse uses an item again, and recycle makes used material into new products.

a.q: Sam washes an empty glass jar and uses it to store pasta. Which action is this?
a.why: The jar is used again as it is, with no breaking down into material. Recycling would mean the glass is processed into new products.

b.q: A café in Orange sends its used aluminium cans to a plant. The plant melts them and makes new cans. Which action is this, and why?
opts: Recycle, because the material is made into new products
Reuse, because the cans are used again as cans
Reduce, because the café now uses fewer cans
Reuse, because the metal is used a second time
b.why: The cans are melted and made into new ones, so the material is recycled. Reuse is the tempting answer, but reuse means using the item again without breaking it down.
b.clue: Was the item used again as it was, or broken down?

b.best: Recycle, because the material is made into new products
